openings.claim: Unreliable addresses may drive repeated searches: retain surname dividers, tie the locator to the reserving reader, and require the clerk to record an exception book's destination before completing its move. Household surnames and stale locations are distinct candidate defects; shelving cart arrivals need not accelerate pickup.
openings.discriminator: Accurate locations with fewer repeat searches supports freshness repair. Remaining searches concentrated on household-name mismatches support identity correction; accurate addresses with peak-window waiting and little search time support the arrival-burst rival. Persistent delays defeat freshness as a sufficient remedy. Cart speed must survive matching arrival volume and book size.
openings.probe: Propose a bounded evening comparison using the sole existing clerk, paper, pencils and timing sheet, two shelves and one cart. Keep names/contact details behind the desk. Record movements, update completion, address accuracy, household mismatches, second searches, arrival, service start, retrieval and completion; compare similar volume, book size and load. Verify recipient identity at each handoff. Count preparation-related corrections within ten daily clerk-minutes, record update workload, and stop if the cap fails; incomplete checks signal feasibility failure.
openings.uncertainty: All observations are synthetic; no benefits are observed. The eight-minute preparation sample plus six post-opening correction minutes does not establish feasible workload. Reservation identity checking and recipient verification capabilities are unconfirmed. Household mismatch causality, cart performance across volume/size, and interview representativeness remain unknown; presence uncertainty is not directly resolved by this proposal. Fixture baseline comparison cannot establish controlled field causality.

lineage.reason: Retains current-address repair, reservation identity, cart counterexample, peak-load rival and capped probe.
Retains movement-completion prevention rule, household-placement rival, feasibility and sufficiency defeats.

decision: Evaluate the merged repair hypothesis conditionally. Require at least 95% of available-hold pickups within two minutes, zero wrong-reader handoffs and every resource/privacy/preparation constraint. Passing a bounded probe would not establish sustained feasibility or causal improvement.
